title: Commands
snippet: Public slash commands with details, required permissions, examples, and prefix syntax. The command list is grouped into Moderation, Economy, Levelling, Games, Music, Configuration, Proxy, Tickets, Global Chat, and Utility.

title: Permission System
snippet: Fine-grained, node-based permissions with hierarchical checking and wildcard support.

title: How It Works
snippet: Ammonite uses a node-based permission system similar to Bukkit/Spigot plugins. Every action is gated behind a permission node (e.g., mod.ban , economy.daily ). Admins can grant or deny these nodes at

title: Permission Hierarchy
snippet: Permissions are evaluated in this order (highest priority first): 1. User-specific 2. Role permissions 3. @everyone 4. Built-in defaults User-specific — permissions set directly on a user always win.

title: Wildcard Permissions
snippet: Wildcard Effect * Grants all permissions (use with extreme caution) mod.* Grants all moderation permissions economy.* Grants all economy permissions economy.games.* Grants all gambling game permission

title: Privacy Policy
snippet: Ammonite is committed to protecting your privacy. Last updated: November 2026.

title: Data We Collect
snippet: Account checks process account-creation time, current username, avatar state, and server join time. Shared suspicious-list records contain user IDs, reasons, and notes; /deletedata removes your entry.

title: How Data Is Stored
snippet: Bot records are stored locally on the bot host machine, kept in memory while the bot runs and persisted locally. No analytics or telemetry is collected. Music commands send search queries or track URLs to the selected provider; Discord interactions, webhooks and ticket messages use Discord's API.

title: Data Retention
snippet: Economy, levelling, moderation, playlist and preference records remain until deleted with /deletedata or removed by the bot operator. Preferences include welcome-DM and account-check choices. Removing the bot does not erase local files.

title: Your Rights
snippet: Use /preference suspicious-checks enabled:false to stop future automatic and manual account checks across servers. It cannot recall prior alerts or remove a shared-list entry.

title: Privileged Gateway Intents
snippet: Guild Members (GUILD_MEMBERS) — role persistence, member joins, welcome messages and moderation member cache. Message Content (MESSAGE_CONTENT) — proxy, prefix commands, global chat and auto-moderation. Presence intent is not used.

title: Global Chat & Webhooks
snippet: The Global Chat feature relays messages between linked channels via Discord webhooks. Relayed messages have a [GC] prefix. Messages are rate-limited and content-capped. Message content is forwarded in

title: Proxy System & Webhooks
snippet: The Proxy system sends messages via webhooks using user-configured display names and avatars. Servers can enable a [proxied] indicator. All proxy data can be deleted at any time by the user.

title: Contact
snippet: Use /deletedata to erase your personal data at any time. Contact the bot owner through the support server or Discord DM. Server owners can contact the bot owner for server-level data requests.

title: Setup Guide
snippet: Add Ammonite to your Discord server and get started in minutes.

title: 1 Invite the Bot
snippet: Use the official invite link to add Ammonite. You must have the Manage Server permission in the target server. Invite Ammonite

title: 2 Grant the Right Permissions
snippet: The invite does not request Administrator. Manage Roles is needed for channel permission overwrites such as /lockdown. Manage Server is only needed for honeypot invite-use detection.

title: 3 Run the Auto-Config Wizard
snippet: Once the bot is in your server, run /autoconfig to launch the setup wizard. It will walk you through everything automatically.

title: Auto-Config Wizard
snippet: The fastest way to configure your server is the auto-config wizard . Run /autoconfig and it will walk you through setting up: Moderation log channel Message log channel Join/leave log channel Suspicio

title: Manual Configuration
snippet: Alternatively, configure individual features with these commands: /settings — general server settings /logging — configure log channels /levels enable — enable the levelling system /points enable — ena

title: Setting Up Permissions
snippet: By default, only basic utility commands are available to all users. To grant moderation access to your staff: # Give moderators all moderation permissions /permissions role-set @Moderator mod.* true #

title: Self-Hosting Guide
snippet: Run your own Ammonite instance from the latest downloadable release. Requires Java 17 or newer and a Discord bot token. Configure bot_name and optional commands, actions, and response lines.

title: Build and Configure
snippet: Download ammonite.jar, create a Discord application and bot, enable the Server Members and Message Content privileged gateway intents, set bot_token in config.json, and run java -jar ammonite.jar.

title: Optional Commands and Response Lines
snippet: Rename slash commands, register aliases and custom commands, configure optional embed_json, pin or react to message IDs, and customize response lines. Each feature is disabled by default.

title: Linux systemd Service
snippet: Download the example systemd unit, create a service account, configure the bot token, enable the service, view journal logs, and restart after updating the JAR.

title: Keep It Running
snippet: Run the JAR from the project directory, monitor logs, and securely back up config.json and the bot's local data.
